verdicts.opus: C and B both grounded their work in the same traced corpus call. C went further: it decomposed critical against total coverage, surfaced dated headlines with URLs, and flagged entity-label artefacts. B gave cleaner exports but misread the censoring and omitted headlines. A and D had no measured data; A declined honestly, while D offered memory estimates about a different quantity.
verdicts.gpt: A is the strongest decision aid: it answers the question with a traced, correctly qualified coverage trend, tone comparison, useful breakdowns, and reproducible exports. C offers broad coverage of facets but misreads the overall direction and censoring, while B and D either rely on estimates or cannot measure the requested reporting pattern.

chatgpt_prism: Treats the May 2026 bucket as censored or partial, when censoring applies from 2026-06-01.
claude_prism: Export is a 6-row subset labelled coverage=full.
claude_bare: Recalled 2022 loss of ~₹7,400 crore likely matches the 2023 figure, so the year appears misattributed (labelled est.).

claude_bare: Presents recalled case counts, loss totals, account blocks, and legal/political developments without resolvable sources; estimates are labelled, but they do not answer the requested corpus facets.

States the headline/publisher matching is central without preserving that the aggregate trend and theme panels use mention matching.

claude_prism.chart: The chart overlays critical on total, but tone is not charted.

chatgpt_prism.trend: Traced monthly series, exact early/late ratio and peak, direction read correctly, and censored endpoint explained; it omits the available critical-series decomposition.
chatgpt_prism.comparison: Same-window topic and corpus negative-to-positive ratios, baseline defined, ratio recomputes, and comparison answers how coverage is framed.
chatgpt_prism.chart: The monthly chart traces to the call and states unit, window, and caption; it does not chart the available critical-share decomposition.
chatgpt_prism.drilldown: Themes and subcategories are described, but item-level headlines lack complete URLs and follow-ups do not cover all open facets.
chatgpt_prism.export: Monthly and publisher CSVs are referenced and carry provenance; monthly values match the source and provenance JSON is included.
chatgpt_prism.repro: Call arguments and window are supplied, numbers trace, derived comparisons recompute, and provenance supports regeneration.
chatgpt_prism.refs: No resolvable article references or source URLs are provided as references.

claude_bare.trend: Only an explicitly estimated recalled series, not the requested digital-arrest coverage series.
claude_bare.comparison: Numeric comparison is explicitly approximate and cannot be checked against the corpus.
claude_bare.chart: Memory-based chart is honestly labelled estimate, earning the estimate anchor.
claude_bare.drilldown: Names generic layers and has some calls, but calls are not executed with non-empty results and breakdown is memory-based.
claude_bare.export: Estimated CSV is labelled and has a window, but lacks a source call and measured provenance.
claude_bare.repro: All figures are estimates from memory; no recorded calls or reproducible source details.

claude_prism.trend: Chart has the full monthly points, but the May 2026 bucket is presented without the required visible censoring and the prose calls the window complete; trend direction is also described as growth in the verdict despite the tool's flat overall direction.
claude_prism.comparison: Tone ratio and corpus baseline are numeric and recompute exactly, with baseline defined; it does not fully address the broader reporting-versus-incidence contrast.
claude_prism.chart: Both series trace, but the window endpoint is misstated, May is not visibly marked censored, and the caption conflicts with the tool's flat direction.
claude_prism.drilldown: One overview layer is presented, but the follow-up calls were not executed successfully enough to meet the traced-layer standard.
claude_prism.export: The CSV is explicitly only a subset of the available monthly data, so it is incomplete for the series the report presents.
claude_prism.repro: Most figures trace, but the window and match-mode claims conflict with the record, and the export omits most monthly rows.
claude_prism.refs: No external references are supplied; headline entries are incomplete and not all have resolving URLs.
claude_prism.accuracy: Calls the measured window complete, claims critical share rose from 80.7% to 94.4% (the cited 80.7% is February 2025, not July 2025), and says headline matching is central though the overview headline feed uses central matching but trends/themes/entities use mention.
claude_prism.limits: Mentions several relevant limits but misstates completeness, censoring, match mode, and the label-fill figure; caveats are not consistently attached to affected numbers.
claude_prism.verdict: The verdict says coverage grew and the window is complete, contradicting the reference's flat overall direction and censored May bucket; it also recommends enforcement priorities beyond what the news data tests.
claude_prism.facets: Addresses most implied facets with grounded values, including trend, tone, themes, geography, sources, entities, and the research/news gap.

chatgpt_bare.trend: No measured series or estimate series is provided.
chatgpt_bare.comparison: No measured comparison or estimate is provided.
chatgpt_bare.drilldown: Only generic proposed follow-ups; no breakdown or executed calls.
chatgpt_bare.repro: No numeric claims to trace and no recorded calls for regeneration.
chatgpt_bare.accuracy: The general scam description does not directly contradict the record; unsupported measurements are explicitly withheld.
chatgpt_bare.limits: Clearly states that no corpus calls were run and identifies what cannot be measured, but has no data-specific window or coverage limits.
chatgpt_bare.verdict: Direct but cautious answer with a decision and confidence; it lacks evidence, contrary findings, and conditions tied to measured data.
chatgpt_bare.facets: Most question facets are explicitly unmeasured, with no grounded corpus values.
